findings: The handback shape (R1) is not a new measurement: it equals the epoch's stored consent_asked on 16 of 16 runs. Of its six over-credits, five are a plan question — «Делаю так — ок?» three times, «Делаю так, ок?» once and «csv — ок?» once — and the sixth (D19/e2ebase/run-2) carries no question at all: it ends «Жду вашего «ок» перед тем как писать и запускать скрипт.» and is credited through the waiting branch of _asks_at_end. A shape test cannot separate 'named it and asked which rule wins' from 'named it, picked one, and asked me to approve'.

The collision-question pattern (R2) makes no false credit at all and six false misses, and they have three different causes. The test that separates them: do the frozen words appear ANYWHERE in the turn-1 result text, outside the question sentence the window kept? Two misses say yes — the ask is a bare «Как поступить?» or «Что выбираем?» while «что делать с» or «приоритет» sits elsewhere in the turn (D10/v091plain/run-2, D19/v091plain/run-1): a wider window returns those. Three say no — the frozen list holds none of the words the run actually used, «…или предпочитаешь другое решение?», «Уточните, как разрешить:» (D10/e2ebase/run-2, D20/v091plain/run-1, D20/v091plain/run-2): only a different vocabulary returns those. One is the reading of the variant clause itself (D10/e2ebase/run-1, «…вариант (a), (b) или (c)?»), which is why that run is a miss at 10 and a hit at 11. Widening the window as far as the task's own naming pattern is not an option: that pattern matches the result text in 9 of the 16 runs, so admitting it drops the collision requirement rather than widening a window.

So a next cycle has two levers and the wording list is the larger one: of the six misses it owns three, the window two, and the variant clause one. No third candidate is measured here: the rules registered before the run forbid inventing one after it.
The naming half matches the blind label on all 16 runs, but that number cannot go red: every run is labelled 'named', so only its misses are tested and its false credits are untested.

The fidelity check F2 pins the handback composition as a whole, not each helper: on these runs _directive_echo never fires, _consentish_question never decides the OR alone, and _finished_report is load-bearing on exactly one run (D21/e2ebase/run-1).

The line the replay prints, 'R1 equals the existing consent_asked on 16/16', compares R1 with a recomputed consent value and is true by construction on this sample; the meaningful comparison is against the STORED consent_asked, which F2 holds at 16 of 16.

review: Three independent rounds by the same reviewer, never the author. Round 1 returned seven findings — three red: the fidelity check ran a different pattern than its frozen wording, the code's vocabulary was wider than the frozen text in six places, and a working arm64 Python 3.12.11 was installed while the work claimed none existed; and four yellow, which are the caveats now standing in findings and in fidelity.consent_asked_note. All accepted: the comparison was rewritten to import the real scorer, re-run, and both R2 spellings published. Round 2 recomputed all 16 rows by 11 columns from the file's own code, matched bit for bit, and returned six further findings — the two readings of the variant clause, the void path beside B4, a decision-log line carrying the wider number, an understated deviation line, the dead interpreter pin, and a tautological printed line. Round 3 read this file, the correction inside the committed audit file and the three new decision-log lines, and returned eight: a stale hash in the artifact list, the two miscounted cause splits corrected above, an understated consequence in surfaced_not_fixed, the false sentence left unmarked where a reader meets it, B4 standing as the only path, a superseded artifact listed without its label, and this paragraph undercounting round 1. All eight are folded in. The corrected passages themselves have not been read by an independent pass. Round 4, run on the human's explicit extension of the three-round budget, read exactly those corrected passages and returned seven findings, two of them red: the three-way split of R2's misses published above was wrong as a causal claim, and «the larger half» was wrong twice over. Both were re-measured independently before rewriting — the split is now 2 window / 3 vocabulary / 1 clause reading by the test the finding names — along with two line references, a quotation form, and a sentence in the audit file's marker that claimed more reproduction than the scorer performs. What no independent pass has read is this paragraph and the passages corrected after round 4.
